utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is cross-examining. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, yesterday I was asking you some questions about the arrival of Mr. Savic and Lugar at your home. Is it fair to say that by the time you left your house and got into the car to head off to Crkvina, you were most reluctant to go out on this venture?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a pleasant experience because I was going off into the unknown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely, so you were reluctant to go. You were anxious about going and you were worried about going and you did not wish to go?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no choice at that point in time, because this was the first time I had heard that I was supposed to go to some sort of Crisis Staff. The two men had arrived, I knew one of them, I didn't know the other one. And when I tried to make a phone call, as I explained yesterday, he almost pushed me away from the phone and said there is no time for that. When you get there, everything will be made clear to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from that that you really didn't want to go and were worried about it, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you had no choice. Is it the fact that Lugar pushed you away from the phone that leads you to believe that you -- makes you say that you had no choice?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think he would have done worse things to me, at least to my way of thinking, had I refused to go with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was simply taken away. I won't say that there was a lot of pressure but they tricked me into going there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the trick?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the trick was in that they didn't tell me why I was going there. They didn't tell me the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say Lugar and Savic were both unarmed, you'd known Savic, so you say, for 20 years. He was in your words a decent, honest family man and performed his job well as a policeman. In those circumstances, if you did not wish to go, it would have been simplicity itself, it would have been really easy, to just say to Savic, "Look, my friend, I don't wish to go out in the middle of the night, I don't want to get involved in this."

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know what there would be when I came there, and Savic wasn't really asked for his opinion. It was Lugar who was in charge of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told -- well, I'll withdraw that. You said in your statement, I believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague but while he is checking his records maybe the witness could have his statement before him. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there was Lugar in charge of things but in your statement, at paragraph 31, you say, that it was Savo who introduced the man and that the man did not talk much on this occasion, it was mostly Savo and I who talked. So how did you conclude that it was Lugar who was in charge, if Savo was the one who brought the man there and Savo was the one who did all the talking?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Lugar kept interrupting Savo Savic and finishing his sentences for him. The way he wanted them to end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggested to you that you knew very well what the purpose of your trip was to Crkvina and that you went willingly with a view to eventually guiding paramilitaries into the town, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you that you knew very well the reason that they had come to your house, you knew that it was to take you to Crkvina and you knew that ultimately your purpose was to guide in the paramilitaries and that you did all of that willingly and happily, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're saying if I had known, but I didn't know. Had I known, I certainly wouldn't have gone there because I know what I went through that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have had to take me by force, had I known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one of the matters mentioned at your house by Savo Savic was that you were a member of a Crisis Staff or the Crisis Staff, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That I was to go to some kind of meeting of a Crisis Staff but I had no idea why or what the purpose and meaning of this Crisis Staff was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Not only that you had to go to a meeting of the Crisis Staff but that you were a member, a member, of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, that I was a member of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at paragraph --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- until that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 32 of your statement, please. Do you see -- do you have it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Third sentence, can you read it out, please, slowly?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Savo told me that he had been told that I was a member of the Crisis Staff and that I was to go to a meeting."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First question, you said in your own statement that Savo told you that you were a member of the Crisis Staff. In court you have just told us that you didn't know that you were a member of the Crisis Staff. Which of those two versions is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this. I object to this. He said I didn't know that, that I was the member of the Crisis Staff and the witness haven't completed his answer and here on line 15, said, until that moment, so there is no inconsistency in his statement before the Tribunal. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well, I'm grateful to my learned friend for pointing that out. I don't want to mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, one thing is for sure. Savo Savic made it clear to you when he came to your house that you were a member of a -- of the Crisis Staff. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did tell me I was a member of the Crisis Staff but I had no idea what the purpose of this was, who the members of the Crisis Staff were, nor did I know anything about it. Why. And who. Nobody asked me if I wanted to be there. So how come I was suddenly in the Crisis Staff? What was the Crisis Staff in Crkvina doing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a good question, isn't it, Mr. Topcagic? Sorry, I didn't wish to interrupt you. If you wanted to say something further, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And why would the Crisis Staff be meeting at midnight? It was all so odd. If I was a member of this Crisis Staff. I did not receive any document telling me about this. I heard about it for the first time that night in my house. I suppose somebody else should have informed me about this, not Savo Savic and Lugar who came to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you've just said that this was all perplexing and bewildering to you so therefore you must have made strenuous inquiries to find out what this membership of this Crisis Staff meant before you got into the car?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So what inquiries did you make?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get any answer from them except what I've just told you, Lugar often used the word "bre," meaning brother, and said, "You have to come now. Everything will be explained to you there. You'll find out everything when you get there. You have to go."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from your answer that you sought some explanation of what this Crisis Staff was but you weren't given one?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the whole conversation led me to believe that I had to go there, whether I wanted to or not, whether I was a member of this Crisis Staff or not. I would have to go, willy-nilly. Perhaps I should say some people know that that night Lugar slapped me, if that means anything to you. I didn't say this before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly didn't. You certainly didn't mention it in your statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention it because I was ashamed. I was 32 or 33 years old and somebody slapped me in my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And this is before, before you're taken off to Crkvina, to this mystery --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason that you didn't mention it in your statement was because of the shame of being slapped by another man, is that -- as I understand what you say.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was ashamed but there was a man who knew about this. It doesn't matter who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But in your statement, in paragraph 33, you do address the issue of your choice, the choice of whether or not you were to go, whether -- the choice of whether you could go to Crkvina or not. You make no mention of this assault, this slap, from Lugar. You were there dealing with this very point?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 33, you talk about how you realised that you had no choice but to go so in your statement you talk about whether or not you had a choice. You're now telling us that the slap by Lugar was one thing that made it clear you had no choice. Why not mention this slap in your statement at that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe we already have the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, Mr. Topcagic has said that he told somebody about this but he didn't mention his name. Maybe we should find out and that would corroborate what the witness has just said. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us whom you mentioned the slap to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it to Simo Zaric, my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider mentioning it in your statement when you were being asked about the events of that night? Or was it shame that prevented you from putting it in?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in the war, I suffered humiliation many times, before the war, I was humiliated by Muslims, during the war by individual Serbs. After the war, by Serbs, Muslims and Croats. Although I helped all these people, and I tried to abide by the ethics of war, to be realistic, I have experienced a lot of things I could tell you about from Stevan Todorovic and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Topcagic but if I want to know about general overview of the war I'll ask you. My question is very simple. At the time that you were writing this statement and talking about the issue of choice, was it shame that prevented you from mentioning the slap? That's all. Just answer that question.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was shame. I was ashamed, because I didn't want someone to gloat over what had happened to me. I remained in the Republika Srpska to fight there and many people gloated over everything I went through, all my misfortunes after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like one small clarification, he said to fight there, to leave there, this is what the witness said. He remained in Republika Srpska to live there. MR. DI FAZIO: I accept what Mr. Lazarevic says. I'm sure he's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn now to the events at Crkvina? When you got there, Savo Savic was still with you? Just tell us yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Savo Savic was not still with me, and I don't know where he went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He drove in the car with you to Crkvina, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, other familiar faces at Crkvina, you knew Todorovic because you recognised him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Todorovic from before the war, because he worked in the Korpara and he was the only one I knew. There were the sareni, the multi-coloured with their faces blackened and there were men with blue berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. So there were men milling about, gathered at the cultural centre in Crkvina and you knew only one of them and that was Todorovic. You didn't recognise a single other person?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recognise a single other person. I didn't go in to the cultural centre. There were probably people inside whom I did know but Stevan Todorovic came out several times and talked to the multi-coloured ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You must have been bewildered and confused and puzzled as to what was going on, having been dragged out of your house at midnight, taken off to Crkvina and surrounded by all these people, none of whom you recognised except for Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dark there. When Todorovic came out, light streamed through the door. I recognised him but I didn't recognise the others. I wasn't so much surprised as afraid, because I didn't know what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you seek an explanation? Perhaps go up to one of these sareni and say, excuse me can you tell me what I'm doing here or what's going on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the courage to do that, because I saw what had happened to me in my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. What about Todorovic? Did you go to Todorovic and say, "Hey, Stiv, can you tell me what's going on? Why am I here?"

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Stevan was an acquaintance of mine, that I had known him when he was working in the Korpara but that we had never spoken until that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the only person you recognised there and you were -- at that moment, you were in a -- let me rephrase that. He was the only person that you knew there who could explain to you what was going on, surely?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I approach him and ask him, Stevo, what's going on, when we hadn't spoken to each other in all our lives. I was fearing that I would experience something even worse than what I had experienced at home, as I said I was afraid. So I didn't ask anything. I didn't dare ask anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was -- I'll withdraw that. Were you under guard? Did someone have a pistol held to your head or a rifle pointed at you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not under guard. They left me in one spot and said I should wait there and not go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider slipping away, perhaps going to the lavatory or wandering off down the road?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even had I done that, what would have happened to me later on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider doing that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did consider it but that would have been very dangerous for me and for my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would it have been dangerous?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because if I had run away, if I fled, my family would not be able to flee. If I went to stay with my family, they would have been able to find me and do whatever they wanted with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that? You didn't even know who these men were, what the purpose -- what purpose they had. You didn't know why you were there. You didn't know what the Crisis Staff was. You knew nothing, according to what you have told us. So where does this supposed fear come from? How can you conclude that if you know absolutely nothing about why you're there or who they are or why they are there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been rumours going around Samac for days that the army from Croatia was to come in and take Samac and Posavina. It was Serbs who talked about this. But Croats and Muslims said that the Serbs were going to invade. There was fear everywhere so I was afraid too, because there had already been an incident in Brod where Croatian forces had entered, killed people, taken Brod, Sijekovac and, well, all sorts of things happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew these weren't Croats, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I knew that because they spoke like people from Serbia. They used the word "bre" a lot. They swore a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Okay, let's move to another topic. At Crkvina, the man you later came to know was Crni divided up the assembled men, the 50 or so assembled paramilitaries into groups, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've just forgotten how many groups. Was it about five or six groups?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were five groups, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And your allotted task was to guide in one of these groups, guide them into town? Correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber who the guides were for the other four groups.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that you couldn't see them or that there were no such guides for the remaining four groups of paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any people and I don't know whether there were guides or not for the other groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the days and weeks following the events of the night of the 16th and 17th, did you ever ascertain if there had been local men guiding in the groups, the other groups, as you did?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you if you were interested. I just asked you if you ever ascertained subsequently if the remaining four groups had used local guides.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see who guided them and I don't know who guided them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew of course their targets, didn't you, the targets of the remaining groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this question. I believe that through the answer that the witness gave that he didn't even know people, whether they were guiding or anything like that, there is no basis for such question. MR. DI FAZIO: There would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lazarevic, the Prosecutor is within his right to ask that question. He's asking about their targets. The witness can answer that. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you knew the targets of the remaining groups?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that they included facilities like the radio station, the post office, yours was the police station, and various other targets including the bridge on the Sava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would -- it was apparent to you then that these men were embarking upon an attack upon the town?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I realised at that point that the town would be attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider saying to Crni, look, please, can you find someone else to do this? For example, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see Mr. Savic around any more and I didn't even know Crni. I only found out several days afterwards who Crni was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You then went into town, in the back of this truck, with these paramilitaries, and you took them to the police station through backyards and unlit streets. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. If I may add something?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived by truck -- a TAM, T-A-M, they put me in the back of the truck, under the canvas. There were five or six of us sitting there. I was the only one wearing civilian clothes. If someone who knew me saw me there in Crkvina, I was wearing jeans and a jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived by truck to the school. Lugar got off the truck and ordered us to get off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topcagic, but I think I'd like to take you to some other areas, if we can. The -- you did your best, didn't you, to take them along the darkest route to the police station? It involved crossing through backyards and going over fences.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, when we set out, they let me walk on my own for about 20 or 30 metres wearing civilian clothes without any weapons because I hadn't taken any weapons, actually I didn't even wear a proper outfit. I didn't know what would happen. I was going there -- I was going as a moving target. I could not dare look behind. Had I done anything, they probably would have killed me, and I mean the Muslim guards, patrols, that were all over town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe this is not what the witness said actually on page 14, line 12. He didn't say had I done anything. He said, had I met anyone. And then I mean the Muslim guards. This gives a sense to this sentence. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. I'm sure Mr. Lazarevic is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was: That you did your best to take them through the most dark and circuitous route to the police station, through backyards, over fences?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to do it for my own sake as well, not only for them, because I was the one there who was in the greatest peril.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then as you arrived at the police station, your choice of vantage point was the flat of Ilija Tolic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you climbed up on to the balcony and you had a good view of the SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was also a wall on the balcony, a good solid wall?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was up on the balcony with you? Was it just Crni or were all of the other paramilitaries up on the balcony with you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to the fence, which we were supposed to jump over in order to enter the yard where the building was, where the TO was, between the TO and the building is a passage way leading to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I've read about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you, Mr. Topcagic, I've read about that in your statement. I know that. You went down the corridor --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You climbed over a fence and you climbed up on to the balcony, the first floor, of Ilija Tolic's flat and stood on his balcony from which you could see the SUP, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, Crni -- you say in your statement that Crni was up there on the balcony with you. All I want to know is was it just you and Crni or were the other paramilitaries also there on the balcony?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this. If my colleague could indicate which paragraph of the statement the witness said that Crni was with him? He haven't mentioned Crni at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, I have a similar question, Mr. Di Fazio. In paragraph 35, it seems that the commanding man was Crni and he told Mr. Topcagic that he was to take away a group whose leader was Lugar. So we don't seem -- so I was going to ask Mr. Topcagic if I could, Mr. Topcagic, was Lugar the leader of the patrol that you escorted to the SUP? Question one. And question two: Was Crni also with you? So was Lugar the one who was assigned to command the patrol that you led into town, first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Crni and Lugar and Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli, were going to the SUP. I didn't know it then but I found out later, as sometime went by, I found out what their names were and that's why I'm putting it this way now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: The second question, Crni was also with you, is answered in the affirmative now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you, because that certainly doesn't appear in the statement. MR. DI FAZIO: No it doesn't. And I also think Mr. Lazarevic was correct when he made his objection. I had been confused between Crni and Lugar. Thank you I'm grateful to Your Honour for pointing those matters out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, up on the balcony, who was with you? Was it just one of these paramilitaries or was the whole group there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the balcony, I mean I had to be the first one to climb up so I did climb up to the balcony and I stayed on the balcony. He walked into the apartment. I don't know who it was. Again one of the many-coloured ones. I can't remember which one of the many-coloured ones it was. And now this passageway between the TO and the building, that's where there were a few more people, that's where Srecko Radovanovic was wounded too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And was he wounded from the blast that struck the police station?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He was not. As a matter of fact, I know who wounded him, if necessary I can mention the name, because I found out about that when I entered the police station. He was wounded by a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded by Salko Hurtic who had threatened me before the war too. He rang my door bell and my wife went out and he said that he would kill me and my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you very much for that. And was he -- he was wounded just outside the police station?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded in the passageway between the TO and that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took them to quite a good position, didn't you, they were up off the ground, they had a good view of the SUP, and they had a balcony wall to protect them from the blast of the explosion that hit the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this question because the witness already said that he was on the balcony and only one paramilitary was together there with him. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Others were on the ground floor in this corridor. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took them to a good position, didn't you? There were -- you and one paramilitary were off the ground, you had a good view of the SUP, the remainder were sheltered in the passageway and that protected them from the blast of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explosion came from the completely opposite side, right to -- to the right from the SUP, from the direction of the memorial [Realtime transcript read in error "policemen orial"] centre. As for this explosion, no one was really endangered by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's go to the police station now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I can just have one small correction for the transcript, on page 18, the direction of the police memorial centre. It was a memorial centre. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we take you to the police station? You're task was complete once you had guided these men to the SUP, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go into the SUP?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the shooting came from the direction of Donja Mahala. It came from the Muslim formations towards the SUP. And after that, gunfire started from Croatia and this gunfire was aimed at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was why did you go into the SUP?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went in because I mean because they ordered me to go in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you seek an explanation as to why you were now being ordered to go into the SUP when you had done your job, you had guided them in?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we entered the SUP, then all hell broke loose there. They immediately started beating the people who were there, people who happened to be at the SUP and people who were arriving then, who did not know that the SUP had been taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any attempt to get out of there? To leave? To get away from this entire scene?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I leave? They would have killed me if I had passed less than 100 metres, either one side or the other side, the many coloured ones they didn't know me for the Muslim formations with which I had so many problems before the war. They would have been after me. Fortunately I did not move about very much and that is how I managed to survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stayed there for your own protection?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where could I go? At 3.00 at night? What time was it? 2.30 a.m., 3.00 a.m., where could I go in the middle of the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where you could go in the middle of the night was to take one of the wounded paramilitaries back to Crkvina in an unmarked police car. You felt safe enough to do that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to do that. It was safer for me to go to drive to Crkvina, that is, than to remain at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why? Why, Mr. Topcagic, why was it safer for you to go in a car away from the SUP building with a paramilitary in your car past these so-called Muslim armed men, to Crkvina? A car can be shot at as well as a person walking down the street, that's elementary. So why was it safer?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, they sent me to sit on some steps facing the Republic of Croatia. There is a big rock there. It goes all the way up like the building does and the shooting started from Croatia straight away. The Croats were targeting the police station and they wouldn't allow me to move from there where bullets were already flying all around me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, I hadn't realised this. You were made into some sort of human shield or placed in this position of extreme danger; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly. From the very beginning of that action that I was taken into, and I was cheated into it actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- I'm not asking you about the whole overview of the situation I'm asking you about the police station. Am I correct that you were taken out the back of the police station --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- facing Croatia and told to stay there as a target?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was some misunderstanding about what the witness said. I believe that the Trial Chamber and my learned colleague watched carefully the videotape containing records on police station. He didn't say he was taken out of the police station and placed there but he said that there is some window or something like that in the police station that can -- so he was inside not outside, nothing more than that. MR. DI FAZIO: Fine, fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to some point in the police station and deliberately exposed to danger, deliberately exposed to Croatian fire?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether it was deliberate or not, I had to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, just tell the Trial Chamber what happened to you in the SUP as regards this incident. Were you taken by paramilitaries to some point in the police station from which you were vulnerable to Croatian fire and as far as you can tell, was that done deliberately? Simple question, just tell the Chamber what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you about what happened at the police station. When I entered the police station, I found that neighbour of mine there, the one I remembered, Salko Hurtic, and he himself said to me that he had fired his weapon, and that he had wounded a person then. He did not know exactly then who it was. And I didn't know at that time either. I told him not to say anything to anyone. They took his rifle away from him. He also had a hand grenade, and he threw it behind the sofa at the duty officers office. When they got in, there were two or three policemen there and they started hitting people straight away. I was frightened. I was upset. I addressed, I don't know who, somebody over there, and I asked what I was supposed to do then, and then Lugar said to me, sit there on the stairs and don't move anywhere. If somebody comes up or something, then I was supposed to inform them. I don't know who he meant who it was who could come up, so I huddled there on the stairs and there is this big glass pane that goes down these steps, and it faces the Republic of Croatia, and that's where bullets started coming from, and I saw -- I heard this conversation over the radio. I don't know who was speaking because the duty officers room is right by these stairs and they were talking to these people from Croatia immediately. They were cursing their Chetnik mothers and these were cursing their Ustasha mothers, and we would be coming, whatever, the entire conversation could be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that, can I conclude, can the Chamber conclude, that you were not placed deliberately in the face -- deliberately in the line of Croatian fire? It was just accidental?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether it was deliberate or whether it was accidental but I was there and there were some expressions --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You drove Debeli, the wounded Debeli back to Crkvina. How badly wounded was he?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded in the shoulder, in the shoulder area. I'm not very knowledgeable as far as wounds go but I just saw that it was bleeding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was he able to walk? Did he have to be placed in the car? Was he able to talk? Was he sitting upright?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could talk. He was sitting sort of on the side and when we arrived in Crkvina, then I helped him a bit. I helped him get out of the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you had seen that night, you knew that the town was under attack and that these armed paramilitaries were taking over the place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew that the 4th Detachment was duty-bound to protect the property and the lives of the citizens of Bosanski Samac? That was one of its objectives?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the 4th Detachment, during this trip back to Crkvina, did you consider trying somehow to raise the alarm with the 4th Detachment? To inform them of numbers of men which you knew? To inform them of the targets of these men which you knew? To inform them of the fact that they came from Serbia, which you knew? To inform them of all of that sort of intelligence so that they could deal with this attack?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I thought about my own survival. I kept thinking about my children all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no doubt you did but did you think of informing the 4th Detachment and passing on this vital intelligence that you had? Numbers, armaments, intentions of this group of thugs who were attacking the town.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what would happen to me when I arrive, what he'd do with me after that. Lugar said already at the SUP, when these bullets were flying all around me, and when I started going down, I wanted to lie down so that nothing would hit me. He said, why are you afraid, Turk? One Turk more, one Turk less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. When you got to Crkvina the second time that night, this is at the cultural hall, you saw Dr. Blagoje Simic and he attended to Debeli, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was inside the cultural centre?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dr. Simic was prepared, apparently, as doctors are, with medical equipment, bandages, whatever was necessary to treat Debeli?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had all of that but the doctor did help Debeli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a field hospital, a small field hospital, not necessarily a full hospital but were there medical facilities set up plainly to treat wounded men?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who else was in the cultural centre? Apart from Debeli and Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a lot of men or were they just a few in number?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't a lot of men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you knew Blagoje Simic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, did you make any inquiries of Dr. Blagoje Simic so that he might explain some of the mysteries that you had seen that night? For example, did you ask him about the Crisis Staff, what it was, why you were a member? You won't find the answer --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider asking?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't consider that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask Dr. Blagoje Simic, "Can you please tell me what's going on?"

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were surely curious to know what was going on, what you'd -- the meaning of everything that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said I was frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I thought of was my family at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes but this was a far different situation, wasn't it? Number 1, the paramilitary, Debeli, was a wounded man; number 2, you're in the company of a doctor, Dr. Blagoje Simic, a familiar face; number 3, you were outside of Bosanski Samac, away from all of this action. This was a completely different scenario, a completely different scene, relatively speaking unthreatening compared to what you had been through. Wasn't that the perfect time to seek some answers to these questions?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, had I perhaps been in another war too, perhaps I would have put that question, but this was something quite new to me. It was something terrible. It was the first time I saw a wounded person. The first time I saw people in camouflage uniforms with paint on their faces, who were beating other people up without asking them anything, who they were, or whatever. People who treated me as if I were a worthless object. I didn't think that they meant anything good. I mean it was my impression that they did not mean any good, did not have good intentions vis-a-vis the Serbs, too, not only the Muslims and Croats, judging by everything that I had seen at that time that was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you left and started to hitchhike back to Bosanski Samac, just prior to leaving, did you receive any further instructions from Debeli?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just said to me that I was free to go, to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you about not passing on information about numbers of paramilitaries, of armament, of any sort of intelligence as to their targets, as to who they were?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say any of the things you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, armed with this very, very good firsthand intelligence regarding the attack that was under way, did you make every effort to get back and report to the 4th Detachment and provide them with this intelligence so that they might perform their duty and protect the citizens and the property in the town?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at Ciglana which is at the entrance to Samac, I went on on foot, as far as the SIT where the command of the 4th Detachment was. There, at the entrance to the command of the 4th Detachment, I met the commander of the 4th Detachment, Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as far as you can tell, you were the only member of the 4th Detachment to have seen part of these takeover events firsthand?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I was the only person from the 4th Detachment who had been at the SUP. I didn't see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you told Antic and Mr. Zaric very briefly what you had been through, what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did tell them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide them with information as to numbers of men, armaments that they were carrying, the intended targets that they had -- just a minute. Just a minute, Mr. Topcagic. Intended targets, armaments, who their leaders were, where they were from? Did you provide them with that information in the very brief conversation that you had with them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them what had happened to me that night, where I had been, how we set out, where we set out, what happened. I said that I assumed these sareni came from Serbia, judging by their dialect and the curses they used, the swear words they used. I told them that and they were surprised and concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But apart from telling them about being from Serbia and swearing and their dialect, did you tell them as to the weaponry they carried, the targets that they carried, the numbers of men that there were, the sort of matters that might interest someone like Radovan Antic and Simo Zaric and other members of the 4th Detachment, the sort of matters that are necessary to deal with an attack?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there were some 50 men there, and as for weapons, they had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Okay. So you made it clear to Mr. Zaric and Mr. Antic that you had good intelligence. Did they or did you suggest that you also go along to the command of the 17th Tactical Group so that you could brief them in good detail as to precisely what was going on, you being the only eyewitness from the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not suggest this. They went on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they didn't suggest it either, Mr. Zaric or Mr. Antic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't suggest it either. I was not in a fit state to go in a car because I was frightened, exhausted and I was not in very good health then, and nor am I in good health now. So I couldn't face driving 40 kilometres to Pelagicevo and then coming back and any way, who was I to go there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your health problems in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have high blood pressure, I have angina pectoris. I have -- my aorta in my heart is enlarged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, that's quite enough. You had these conditions in 1992, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell the Chamber how you went leading this group of paramilitaries jumping over fences, in this stressful situation? Did any of your -- suffer any health problems?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am ill but I live with this disease. I don't let it burden me too much. When I jumped over the fence, and that too is something that is not in this record, Lugar hit me on the back with the barrel of his rifle, because they wanted me to jump over the fence and there was a dog tied up on the other side and the dog was barking and jumping up against the fence. As I didn't want to jump over, he hit me with the gun barrel, with a rifle barrel on my back, and then they helped me to jump over the fence. I could have jumped it myself but I was scared of the dog, and of what was awaiting me further on, because then I would have to go forward again some 10, 20 metres ahead of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, have you ever found out in all these years who it was who made the choice of you to guide in a group of paramilitaries in the middle of the night? Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Because simply had anything happened to me, they wouldn't have been very sorry. Many people would not have regretted it. I'm speaking of Serbs and especially of Muslims who represent a special story in my life, and the Croats least of all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's jump a few topics to the situation on the morning of the 17th. Men started -- men from the 4th Detachment started to arrive at the headquarters at the SIT factory, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some in uniform, some not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some armed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they all arrived there presumably with different methods, some walked, some took their bicycles, some may have taken cars?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had already gathered there, I didn't see how they arrived. The ones who lived closest to the command of the 4th Detachment were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did any of the un-uniformed, men not in uniform, from the 4th Detachment engage in any fire with the Serbian paramilitaries that morning?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state with full responsibility that no one from the 4th Detachment fired a single bullet. I assert this because those were the orders before the detachment commander, the commander of the 4th Detachment, Radovan Antic came back and nothing was to be done, except to gather as many men as possible and wait for further orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting by the Muslim side, and the first shots hit perhaps the house of Miroslav Tadic. We could see that from the yard of the SIT.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And they were Muslims who shot at the house of Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had some sort of green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not camouflage uniforms? You know what a green uniform is and you know what a camouflage uniform is. Were they in camouflage or green uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, green uniforms and some of them also had camouflage uniforms but later they got rid of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you recognised --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, the camouflage uniforms came from the HVO and they were worn by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw these men shooting at Mr. Tadic's house and you recognised them as being local Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see but I know where the shots came from, from the stadium, from the stands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, three or four questions ago I asked you they were Muslims who shot at the house of Miroslav Tadic. You said correct.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you say that you didn't see -- you didn't see but you know where the shots came from. Tell the Chamber, these -- take it step by step. There were Muslims who shot at the house of Miroslav Tadic, correct or not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We assume that this is correct, and I am sure. I can guarantee that they shot. I can even give you the names of the people who fired shots. One among them was Dervis Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're absolutely certain that it was local Muslims who shot at the house of Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was no one else who could have done it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this was known to Mr. Tadic, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably knew, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't -- it wasn't just you who knew that local Muslims had shot at Mr. Tadic's house? It was many other men in the 4th Detachment who knew that local Muslims had shot at Mr. Tadic's house?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't actually see the men who shot at Mr. Tadic's house? Didn't lay eyes upon them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them, but that morning, nobody from the 4th Detachment fired a single bullet. The Muslim formations were roaming around the town holding certain parts of the town, and the stadium is a very suitable place to fire from with artillery weapons. On the entire surrounding area. Because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects herself, infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's closer to the headquarters of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... transcript on page 31, line 24, fire from infantry weapon and not artillery weapon. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These light weapons or are we talking heavier weapons that the Muslims had?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Light weapons, infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so let me get this straight. These Muslims are going around town, we know that they fire at Miroslav Tadic's house and that they are firing from the stadium. What were they firing at? I mean apart from Mr. Tadic's house, of course.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that morning, the first shooting started from Donja Mahala, which is at the exit from Samac. That part of the town is called Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And they actually controlled part of the town, actually took control, the Muslims took control of Donja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did offer resistance in Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Resistance to whom?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sareni. MR. DI FAZIO: Is this time, if Your Honours please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will take our break and continue at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, essentially your position is that Muslim forces carried out battles or street -- small fire fights with the paramilitaries and for some period of time, actually controlled parts of the town?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And how long would you say that went on for, a few hours at least?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that shooting could be heard until about 10.00 a.m. that morning, the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no doubt about it, that was fighting between Muslim forces on the one hand and the Serbian police and paramilitaries on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P138 ter? Thank you, Mr. Usher and may I ask you, please, Mr. Usher to open the exhibit to page 34? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Topcagic, that's an interview conducted with Mr. Miroslav Tadic in March of 1998. You will see that it provides his interrogators questions with a B/C/S translation and his answers followed by the B/C/S. At the very top of the page, you will see the top third of the page, that Mr. Tadic is describing the takeover. He says, it was not a problem to take over Bosanski Samac. Do you see that paragraph? MR. DI FAZIO: May I approach the witness to indicate so we don't waste too much time on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, that's Mr. Tadic, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, commenting on the takeover of Bosanski Samac. He says it took half an hour, no -- without shots being fired, without shelling, without bombarding, and then when he's asked by his interrogator if there was no resistance, there was no resistance offered by the non-Serbs --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to what I read in transcript, maybe he could say again what he has just said about what he understood. MR. DI FAZIO: The wrong page is being shown, the wrong page. 35 was being shown. 34. I'm sorry if I said 35.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't mark the exhibit, if you don't mind, Mr. Topcagic,. It's a court exhibit. All right, now do you see the passage that I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, who was there in April of 1992, takes the view that the takeover was not a problem, done in half an hour, no shots fired, no shelling, and then when asked about resistance offered by non-Serbs, comments, "Mostly no resistance, perhaps partly some, but not significant." That contrasts with your evidence. Now, having seen what Mr. Miroslav Tadic said about the takeover, do you now think that in fact the takeover was conducted swiftly, with minimal resistance, and little exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no major resistance, but I can guarantee that shooting could be heard around 10.00 too. I don't know who was doing the shooting then though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that. I'm finished with that exhibit. Thank you. I'm going to have to jump to another topic later in time. You describe in your statement -- I withdraw that. Do you know a fellow named Stevo Milicic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Stevo Milicic. M-i-l-i --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevo Milicic? I don't know that man. Perhaps you mean another Stevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I just want to know. Do you know a fellow named Milan Milicic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That name doesn't mean a thing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of either of those two men ever -- well, you're not aware of a man surnamed Milicic being a member of the Crisis Staff at any point?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Milicic is probably from the village of Pelagicevo. Except that I don't know whether his name is Milan or Stevo. I think the name is Milan Milicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this fellow was a member of the Crisis Staff, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't see him at the Crisis Staff. I've just remembered now that he was on the Crisis Staff too. I remember now his name and surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown P127, please? Now, as far as this document -- as far as this document is concerned, as far as -- all I need to do is ask you to go to the back of the document and you'll see that it's signed by 13 people. The one I'm interested is number 13, Corporal Milan Milicic, assistant commander for civilian -- for civilian affairs, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, being a military man and being in charge for civilian affairs, am I right that it's probably this fellow who was on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's the man. I know that there was some Milicic from Pelagicevo who was on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the fellow that you knew from Pelagicevo who was on the Crisis Staff was a military man, was in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I've done with that document. And can the witness now be shown Exhibit P124?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Topcagic, just while the document is being brought before you, in terms of a person with the surname Milicevic, did you know whether a man called Cedo Milicevic was on the Crisis Staff as a person concerned with security matters? So the first name Cedo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know Cedo Milicevic. But he was born in Gornja Slatina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't think so. I know that he was in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is the gazette, the Official Gazette of the municipality of Samac dated June of 1994, and contains a record of a number of decisions. I'd like you to look at a decision dated the 28th of March, 1992, the usher I believe has the document open at the correct page. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it's page 14 of the English translation and I believe page 8 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you just want me to read Article 1 of the decision? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, sorry, could we have it on the ELMO for the benefit of our clients? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it's only one very minor aspect of this document that I'm interested in and, yes, please place it on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Article 1, in the right-hand column --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness have the document before him. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then thereafter you can put it on the ELMO because there are such small letters. MR. DI FAZIO: I realise that, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Article 1, the last sentence of Article 1 says that "The municipal crisis staffs shall be composed of representatives of political, military and other institutions of the Serbian people." Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just read this, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, I'm sorry if I jumped the gun.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I've finished with the document. So it's your position that you are not aware of any requirement that military -- that the military have a representative on the Crisis Staff? Am I correct? You don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Now let's go to the occasion that you attended at the Crisis Staff meeting. The men that you saw there, these men, Simeon Simic, Todorovic, Blagoje Simic, Milos Bogdanovic, and Bozo Ninkovic, all of them were not --

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo Popovic was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Savo Popovic. All of them were not members of the 4th Detachment; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was there except for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. It's just the way it was translated there is a little bit of uncertainty. What you meant to say was that you were the only 4th Detachment person at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the only person. I don't know how come I was there in the first place, how come I was elected, how come I was actually nominated, because this was the only meeting I attended, and never again after that. I was never invited. I never received any compensation for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Fine, fair enough. I hear what you say. But my question is this: You were the only 4th Detachment person present?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was very soon after the 16th and the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps after three or four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the military representative on the Crisis Staff, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a representative of the military. I'm telling you now. I don't know who put me there. I don't know what I was doing there. And I was no important person. I did not decide anything. I did not take part in the discussion. I stayed briefly. I didn't even stay until the end of the meeting. It was Crni and Stevan Todorovic who were doing most of the talking at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I put to you that you were the -- MR. DI FAZIO: Will Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Crni doing there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came, he was there at the meeting. All the discussion that was there, if anybody would start taking part in the discussion, he would interrupt and he would make decisions on his own. He would do the deciding. What was discussed was the situation at that moment in Samac, the shelling, there was no water, there was no electricity in town, how to resolve these problems and then also food supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to suggest to you that in fact you were the military representative, the 4th Detachment representative, or JNA representative, on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was already suggested to the witness and he gave the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer again. I was -- MR. DI FAZIO: All right, fair enough as long as there is no problem with my not putting my case to the witness, I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who told you to go to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Policemen came, a policeman came to fetch me, and told me to go to Uniglas to attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell your superiors, Mr. Antic, perhaps Mr. Tadic, Mr. Zaric, that you were going to a meeting of the new civilian administration? Did you inform them of that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not tell them about that when this policeman came he came by car and I got into the car with him and I went to this meeting. I didn't even know what the point of this Crisis Staff was, what it was for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was that -- this was the second time that the mystery of the Crisis Staff had come before you, wasn't it? The first occasion was when you were informed that you were a member of the Crisis Staff on the night of the 16th and 17th and now for a second time this issue of the Crisis Staff had arisen, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first time they told me that I was going there to some Crisis Staff, and there was no Crisis Staff there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Did you ask the policeman why you were going or why you were required?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he just told me that I was supposed to go, that they were calling me to come there to the Crisis Staff and he didn't do any other explaining. And then when I asked him who was there and he said, I have no idea I was just instructed to bring you there, I was instructed by Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you got to the Crisis Staff and you saw these assembled men, did you ask any of them, "What am I doing here? Why am I here?"

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was too big a bite for me. I couldn't wait to leave. There were other people there who were more important than me, and who did not really feel very comfortable in the presence of Crni, let alone Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. When you say it was too big a bite for you, do you mean that you felt intimidated? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, to encounter Stevan Todorovic meant pure evil. It didn't matter whether it was me or anybody else. He did a lot of evil to a lot of people regardless of whether they were Muslims or Croats, honest Serbs, too, everybody had a problem with him so as soon as I saw him, everything became black to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. But I mean, at that stage of events, Mr. Todorovic had not yet got into full swing, had he? It was still too early for you to know that that he was the sort of person he later turned out to be?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right away, he locked up some 50 Muslims in the TO, and when beating began and forcing people to sing Chetnik songs and many other things that nobody likes to mention, and the things he did in the SUP, in front of the policemen and those people, to show them what things should be like, what a real Serb should be like, evil news spreads quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I see, so the evil of Mr. Todorovic was a factor -- was a fact that was already well known in Bosanski Samac to someone like you, who was not even associated with the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at all associated with the civilian authorities. When I went to the Crisis Staff meeting, I was surprised by that, and I never wanted to go there again, and they never actually invited me again, but even had they done so, I would not have gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, I suggest to you that there couldn't have been too much fear and intimidation on your part because firstly, you had assisted these paramilitaries, you'd performed this dangerous job of guiding them in to the city, successfully, taking them to the police station, and secondly, here they were inviting you to this meeting. So there couldn't have been too much of an atmosphere of menace for you, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not agree with what you said, because first I was slapped, then I was hit on the back with a rifle barrel, then I was made to sit on the steps with bullets whizzing around me. You can draw your own conclusions from that. Whether I was privileged in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you introduced to the assembled people, the assembled men?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in the meeting altogether?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there for about an hour and a half and then I left because I had to go to the front line, about an hour and a half, maybe a little less, maybe a little more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you participate in the meeting? I mean apart from your presence, did you engage in discussion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not participate in the discussion. I just told them I had to go to the front line. As I said, it was Crni and Stevan Todorovic who did most of the talking, at least while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told the Chamber that what was being discussed were domestic problems, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
